nodes.summary: The model checking, satisfiability and validity problems of the linear modal μ-calculus are PSPACE-complete, like for linear temporal logic. Source: M. Y. Vardi, "A temporal fixpoint calculus", POPL 1988, 250-259; cf. A. P. Sistla and E. M. Clarke, "The complexity of propositional linear temporal logics", JACM 32 (1985), 733-749.
nodes.title: The model checking, satisfiability and validity problems of the linear modal μ-calculus are PSPACE-complete

nodes.summary: Model checking of the linear μ-calculus as a decision problem over bitstrings: the input decodes to `(n, edges, worldVals, start, tokens)`, where `worldVals` lists, per world, the atoms true at that world; the answer is whether the decoded formula is closed, the structure is well-formed and total (every world has a successor world, so the path quantification is not vacuous at deadlocks), and every path from `start`…
nodes.title: Linear μ-calculus model checking as a decision problem

nodes.summary: Model checking a linear μ-calculus formula against a finite Kripke structure: every infinite path `π` from `start` following `edges` satisfies `φ` at position `0`, where the path turns the structure's valuation `worldVal` into a word valuation.
nodes.title: Linear μ-calculus model checking on a finite Kripke structure

nodes.summary: Satisfiability of the linear μ-calculus as a decision problem over bitstrings: the input decodes to a formula token list, which decodes to a formula; the answer is whether that formula is closed and satisfiable.
nodes.title: Linear μ-calculus satisfiability as a decision problem

nodes.summary: A closed linear μ-calculus formula is satisfiable: some word and position satisfy it under the empty environment.
nodes.title: Satisfiability of a closed linear μ-calculus formula

nodes.summary: Validity of the linear μ-calculus as a decision problem over bitstrings.
nodes.title: Linear μ-calculus validity as a decision problem

nodes.summary: A closed linear μ-calculus formula is valid: every word and position satisfy it under the empty environment.
nodes.title: Validity of a closed linear μ-calculus formula

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
